issues.description: The deletePerson method signature differs between template, solution, and the described REST endpoint: the problem statement and template expect deletion by UUID (DELETE /persons/{personId}), template's PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId), and PersonResource (solution) calls personService.deletePerson(personId). However the solution's PersonService incorrectly defines deletePerson(Person person). This mismatch prevents the server code from compiling and contradicts the described API contract (deleting by personId).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the PersonService.deletePerson method accept a UUID (UUID personId) and remove the person by matching id, matching the template and the REST endpoint. For example: public void deletePerson(UUID personId) { this.persons.removeIf(person -> person.getId().equals(personId)); } Adjust any callers if necessary so that PersonResource calls this method with the personId path variable.

issues.description: The DELETE /persons endpoint in the problem statement and the template expects deletion by UUID (personId), and the template's PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId). In the solution, PersonResource calls personService.deletePerson(personId) but PersonService in the solution defines deletePerson(Person person). This creates an unintentional identifier/parameter-type mismatch between the REST resource and the service layer (UUID vs Person) that will confuse students and cause compile/runtime errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the service method signature with the endpoint contract. Change the solution's PersonService.deletePerson(Person person) to deletePerson(UUID personId) (matching the template and the REST resource), and implement removal using the UUID. Alternatively, if deleting by Person is intended, update PersonResource to resolve and pass a Person object, but the simpler fix is to use deletePerson(UUID personId) to match the problem description and template.
